title: do/catch with Multi-Pattern Catches

docs.title: Error Handling — Handling Errors Using Do-Catch

hints: A `catch` clause can list several patterns and bind associated values.
Call `try buy(request)` in a `do`, then add catches for the two "unavailable" cases together, the funds case, and a bare `catch`.
`catch VendingError.invalidSelection, VendingError.outOfStock { return "unavailable" }` and `catch VendingError.insufficientFunds(let needed)`.
jsBridge: `catch VendingError.invalidSelection, VendingError.outOfStock` matches several patterns in one clause. JS has a single untyped `catch (e)` followed by `if` chains; Swift's catch clauses are pattern matches.

compass.q: JS has one `catch (e)`. How many `instanceof` checks does this Swift code replace?
Must a `do/catch` be exhaustive? What happens to errors no clause matches in a throwing vs non-throwing function?
`catch let e as VendingError` vs `catch VendingError.x`: when does each fit?
Network errors (`URLError.notConnectedToInternet`) are commonly matched this way. Which URLError codes deserve special UI?
